findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `gate_run.status` (and `verdict`) value vocabulary in the new schema — enumerate running/passed/failed/attaching/unknown (and the verdict members) or state explicitly why these stay unconstrained strings.
evidence: Runtime gate_run_status returns status in {running, passed, failed, attaching, unknown} (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:324-325)
The gate_status tool docstring branches on these exact tokens: 'Status is running, then passed or failed … attaching awaits … unknown marks an unrecognized ID' (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:203-207)
Precedent schemas enumerate such fields: gate_result.verdict enum [pass,fail]; transition_result.completion_signature.cause enum (gate_result.schema.json:10, transition_result.schema.json:22)
Plan text names `status` but assigns no enum/vocabulary
findings.finding: The new `gate_run` schema (tool `gate_status`) declares a `status` field whose value vocabulary is never defined, though it is bounded and branched on by callers.
scenarios: An LLM/MCP client polling gate_status cannot rely on a declared vocabulary and may mishandle 'attaching' (keep-polling) vs 'unknown' (terminal)
Executor cannot tell whether to emit an enum constraint or a bare string, risking the same drift the mirror caused
findings.suggested_fix: Add `"status": {"type":"string","enum":["running","passed","failed","attaching","unknown"]}` to gate_run.schema.json, and either enumerate `verdict`'s members or document why it is left open.

resolve_symbol confirms mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP and mcp.server.lowlevel.server import, but neither resolve_symbol nor public docs confirm the fn_metadata attribute names or that output_schema is a writable post-registration hook.
Repo-scoped tools cannot read site-packages (venv is outside repo root), so these internals are unknowable from the plan text alone — a load-bearing, version-sensitive assertion.
Plan says the list-wrapping RootModel path was 'prototyped', which does not cover the output_schema rebind / output_model+wrap_output assertion.
findings.finding: The installer's core mechanism depends on undocumented private SDK internals — mcp._tool_manager.get_tool(name).fn_metadata.output_schema and the fn_metadata.output_model / wrap_output attributes with the asserted semantics (wrap_output == (kind != 'object')) — but the plan grounds only the public lowlevel jsonschema.validate call with a file:line, leaving the actual rebind path an unverified capability assertion pinned implicitly to mcp 1.29.0.
